relationships.description: The transition is fired by the UI event that this action control emits, linking the button, link or menu entry the user activates to the state change it causes.
relationships.evidence: The state machine definition names the transition's event (e.g. 'SUBMIT') and the component's onClick handler sends that same event, as in an XState send('SUBMIT') call bound to the button.

relationships.description: When the transition fires, the experience leaves its owning state and becomes the destination state, which then governs which components are enabled, disabled or hidden.
relationships.evidence: The transition entry in the machine config declares a target, e.g. on: { SUBMIT: { target: 'submitted' } }, and that target names a state defined in the same machine.

relationships.description: Firing the transition runs this side-effect action, such as submit, validate or dispatch, as part of its ordered on-transition action list.
relationships.evidence: The transition's actions array in the machine config lists the action by name, e.g. actions: ['validateForm', 'submitOrder'], and that name resolves to an implementation in the machine's actions options.

relationships.description: The transition borrows this shared motion definition to animate the UI's change from the source state to the destination state, taking its animation type, duration and easing from the template.
relationships.evidence: The transition's spec or component code references the template by identifier, e.g. transition: 'fadeSlide', and the referenced definition lives in a shared motion or animation config module.

notes: navigates-to is a questionable predicate here: it is catalogued as UI navigation between screens or routes, while ExperienceState is explicitly not a screen or route. A dedicated 'targets-state' predicate, or flows-to, would fit better. associated-with to ActionComponent is vague; 'triggered-by' would express the event-source role more precisely.
